In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: (i) WIMP annual modulation search; (ii) search for rare events (e.g. solar axions); (iii) search for double-beta decay; (iv) study of low energy processes in NaI(Tl).

the study of the annual modulation signature of Dark Matter in the galactic halo, as predicted by the so-called DAMA/NaI and DAMA/LIBRA annual modulation results, and with the study of a number of other possible Dark Matter signatures.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DAMA/LIBRA data are in agreement with the expected modulation signature and the model of the WIMPs annual modulation signature is compatible with all data.

the model independent positive results obtained by DAMA/NaI and DAMA/LIBRA experiments are not in disagreement with the results of other direct detection experiments and with the results of the CERN-LHC, Fermilab, SuperK and other experiments.
the DAMA/LIBRA data are compatible with the presence of DM particles in the Galactic halo on the basis of all the criteria required by the Standard Model of Cosmology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DAMA experiment has provided the first and still the only evidence for the presence of Dark Matter in the Universe in the direct detection field.
we have achieved the best results in the field, both from the experimental point of view and for the obtained sensitivity.

the DAMA experiment is now the only one to have clearly detected a signal with high significance (more than 8σ) and compatible with the expected signature from WIMPs in a model independent way, and that this signal is in agreement with all the other results obtained by the experiment in the field of the Dark Matter search.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have observed an annual modulation in the NaI(Tl)-scintillation rate, with all of the characteristics expected if the effect is caused by WIMPs.

the annual modulation effect has been clearly observed and that the modulation signal is highly significant (more than 8.2σ) in the energy interval 2-6 keVee, where the expected WIMP-induced event rate is maximum.
the DAMA/LIBRA annual modulation results are still in full agreement with those of the other direct detection experiments.
